invariants.rationale: It is common (but not required) for array-typed arguments to be non-null, especially when they represent a set of options for internal logic. The method assigns this to a field, so callers likely intend to provide an initialized array.
Java arrays always have a non-negative length, so this is a safe invariant if autocompleteOptions is not null.
If autocompleteOptions is null, accessing the length would throw, so this safely expresses non-negative length when array is non-null.
If autocompleteOptions is non-null, it is guaranteed to be an array.
